Breaking: A new report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a latest report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work.
  • That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.
  • Industry observers note that the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a latest report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

Industry observers note that the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a big split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

In a recent development, there seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

Recent findings suggest that what is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

Industry observers note that "I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," said one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota.

The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with substantial companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

Crimson Desert studio is implementing AI "throughout our entire development pipeline," and expects DokeV to launch in 2028

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.
  • The South Korean studio mentioned as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".
  • "However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

The South Korean studio mentioned as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

"However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer said.

In a recent development, when Crimson Desert first debuted, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before promptly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

It seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously.".

In a recent development, elsewhere in the letter, the studio remarked its previously confirmed creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year.".

Industry observers note that the use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and big companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to.
  • In a recent development, in addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold.

Sources indicate that gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest upgrade post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In a recent development, in addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by Newly introduced Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Other than these newly introduced hires, the update is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

The patch is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but Newly introduced Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next.
  • Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis said in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

It has been revealed that "I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in newly introduced players.'".

The Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each latest entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis said.

"This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty substantial gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

Industry observers note that it was a success so significant it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have no desire to be an iconoclast.
  • I’ve always playedÂ GTA games on PC.
  • In a recent development, except, is that even realistic this time?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Rockstar.

I have no desire to be an iconoclast. Today’s launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is by far the biggest release in all of gaming history, and on pre-orders alone it’s already the biggest game of 2026. It’s the most expensive game ever made, and it seems inevitable that it’ll be the highest-grossing game ever released. Not only that, but it’s also extraordinarily good. It’s a pinnacle in gaming, and it’s going to be the focus of the worlds I exist in for months to come. Of course I want to be a part of this. But I also want to playÂ GTA 6 for the first time on PC.

I’ve always playedÂ GTA games on PC. Partly because I sometimes didn’t own the relevant PlayStation at the time, and partly because the first 20 years of my career were primarily spent covering PC games. But also because the PC versions were always better. That’s not some silly factional position, or dumb anti-console nonsense, but rather just a statement of fact. Rockstar would put out the console version, then spend six months removing all the artificial limitations and adding all the features that had remained stuck on wish lists, and then let the game loose into the unfettered technology of personal computing. The PC release is always the definitive version of any Grand Theft Auto, complete with six months of bug fixes on top of the myriad improvements, and what better way to first experience a great game than in its finest form?

In a recent development, except, is that even realistic this time? Let’s entirely put aside the notion that as some manner of “games journalist,” it’s arguably important that I be culturally aware of the biggest game release ever. I’m also a person who wants to enjoy a game in the way he wants to enjoy it. But dear god, the pressure to play the moment my clock hits midnight. Heck, for me that’s five hours earlier than it is for folks in the U.S.! I’ll be ahead of the curve! And everyone else I know will be playing this game in every moment they can. The mimetic pressure alone is overwhelming.

This time I certainly do own the console, and although my PS5 doesn’t get a lot of use (here again I appear to have accidentally gone against the curve, but I just find my Xbox Series S and Game Pass to be a much more attractive prospect), it’s there and ready to offer me a game that a few of my colleagues have already finished and assure me I’m going to adore. And I want to be adoring it! Zack’s review is making this all the harder for me, as he so beautifully describes the minutiae of the game, the smallest details that seem so deeply attractive. I’m so astonished to learn that each of the two main characters has their own distinct social life, and can get up to their own business while you’re playing as the other. I want to experience that! And I can, in just 12 hours’ time. But…I want to experience it at its best, and I can’t for at least five more months.

It has been revealed that I’m so torn! There’s absolutely no part of me that thinks it’s somehowÂ interesting to not play GTA 6. Ooh, look at me, the artisan gamer in his beret as he plays an obscure Welsh-language art-house experimental game that muses on the notion of grief and ontology, and not yourÂ mainstream gaming. No, not that at all. I just want the first time I play the incredible game to be as incredible as possible, and I know that the PC version will be a substantial step up, even from the incredible application of six-year-old tech on display in the PS5 version. The PC version will be designed to use day-old tech, pushed to work with the most recent graphics card and RAM you’ve been able to cobble together, and heck, it might even run at over 30 FPS.

Recent findings suggest that but I’m not even driven by the tech. I just…like playing games on PC. It’s the machine I played games on as a teenager, and the machine that gave me a career writing forÂ PC Gamer and foundingÂ Rock Paper Shotgun. I love my PC. I like playing games at my desk, on my ultra-wide monitor, whether I’m using mouse/keyboard or a console controller. I get curling up on the couch and enjoying games that way, but there’s something about the intimacy of the screen being two feet from my face, not the other side of the room, that draws me further in. There are fewer distractions in my teeny office, carved into messy shape over years of gaming and working. And that’s another thing! It’s a far safer way to play a game like GTA 6 when there’s a 12-year-old in my house who cannot comprehend why I might not want him watching, let alone playing. A 12-year-old who wants to be camped in the same room as my PS5, playingÂ Minecraft on his Switch while on the phone to the other kids in the same realm. That’s no place for some 18+ gaming entertainment.

Sources indicate that so what should I do? I still don’t know. My instinct is that I’m going to give in, fork out the Â£70 ($92) for a copy, and then be really annoyed with myself whenever the PC version does come out. I’ll have only been able to play the PS5 version in fits and starts, given the availability of the living-room TV and the appropriateness of who else is in the room, or I may sacrifice any notion of sleep and play the game nocturnally, frustratedly squinting to read the inevitably tiny text on the more distant television, knowing that it just won’t be the same to play it over again. But if I don’t, obviously everything that’s still a surprise will have long been spoiled for me by the time I play, and I’ll be missing out on the excited conversations of friends and colleagues who will be sharing amazing moments and crucial discoveries.

Industry observers note that bigger than that, I’ll not be part of the cultural zeitgeist, this enormous moment of shared entertainment that will beÂ everywhere, referenced inÂ everything, and by all accounts, utterly, stunningly good. And that sucks. But [wrinkled nose, sulky tone] I want to play to play it on PC. I just wanna. It’s not fair. I’m completely stuck about what to do.

GTA 6 Has an Easy Mode Buried in an Impressive Range of Accessibility Options

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.
  • There's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable.
  • But there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.

There's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable. And while the initiative isn't quite as in-depth as what you'll find in recent Ubisoft or Sony-published titles, it's still a solid step forward for the studio.

But there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows. As you might know, Rockstar never deals in difficulty levels; outside of things like adjustable aim assist, you're always in line with the developer's intended challenge.

In GTA 6, however, there are two difficulty-related toggles buried in the accessibility options: 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage'.

It has been revealed that in essence, both settings amount to having an easy mode. Accessible Combat decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.

Meanwhile, Reduced Vehicle Damage does exactly what it says on the tin, making your chosen ride more durable.

But just how much easier do these toggles make GTA 6? The options menu itself complications a warning, stating that when enabled, the "balance and experience" of the game is "significantly" changed.

We've put them to the test, and despite some claims I've seen floating around the internet this morning, they do not make you invincible. You still need to play the game as intended — actually taking cover in firefights, for example — but the overall level of challenge is still noticeably reduced.

The idea is that these toggles will allow less experienced, mentally fatigued, or disabled players to progress without too much friction.

Industry observers note that and just to be clear, enabling these settings does not disable Trophies. The bottom line here is that if you're having trouble getting through GTA 6, these options should almost certainly help.

Speaking of help, you can check out our overall GTA 6 guide and our totally spoiler-free Tips & Tricks guide for assistance with everything from collectibles to neat gameplay features you may not know about.

It has been revealed that as for the other accessibility settings on offer, Rockstar's covered a lot of ground. For starters, there are a bunch of aim assist and lock on options, while button taps and presses can be customised to an impressive extent, to make them less physically demanding.

You can even toggle "simplified" minigames, making the controls less complex, and there are multiple ways to customise controller layouts.

On top of that, a multitude of low vision options are available, there's a one-toggle brightness modifier, and there's a dedicated high contrast setting. Again, it's good stuff from the developer.

Have you been adjusting any of these options for your playthrough of GTA 6? Are you happy to see Rockstar adopting a more accessible approach? Snap to your target in the comments section below.

Recent findings suggest that so you've played through the GTA 6 intro, gotten to know Jason and Lucia a bit, and probably been taught how to drive, shoot, and change clothes. You finally reach that moment in an open world game where, for the first time, you're let off the rails to just be.

That's what I want to know, because I suspect we all have a different system or detail that we've been thinking about since the first GTA 6 trailers and leaks—a test we must conduct to determine if "Rockstar really thought of that." I'm talking about hoops shooting, snack eating, or going on a classic GTA rampage.

Sound off in the comments below (there's a button at the top of the page to skip straight to them) to share your night one plans.

According to recent reports, I'm gonna punch someone in the face. I swear I'm not usually one to play Rockstar games like a psychopath, but a bit of random crime will answer a question I've had about GTA 6 for months now: Is evading cops actually interesting? Gameplay leaks suggest that Rockstar has implemented a proper stealth suite with threat indicators and search zones. We also learned that law enforcement will be able to identify Jason and Lucia based on what they were wearing and driving while raising a ruckus. That sounds super interesting, and I can't wait to put those systems through their paces.

I'm going shopping! Actually, I'll probably need some cash first. I will do some crime, and then I will go on a lovely shopping spree. Dressing up my digital counterparts is the main reason I play videogames, mostly because it means that, at least for a few hours, I'm not spending real money on real trainers or the high-quality fabrics that I love to drape over myself.

Going for a drive. I'm also a sucker for playing Barbie with my GTA protagonists, but something I'm really looking forward to is jumping in a car and going for a long drive while cycling through Leonida's radio stations. Rockstar always has an excellent ear for music curation, and there's something about speeding down a highway on a rainy night that hits different. With GTA 6's map being Rockstar's biggest yet, there should be a whole lotta asphalt for me to explore.

Industry observers note that walking off into the woods. I shall find the first tree line and B-line towards it. What interests me more than the cars or even the crime is finding out what kind of wildlife will populate the stretches of land in Leonida. Ever since I heard about the wildlife logbook that Jason (and presumably Lucia) has access to I've been planning my nature excursion, someone's going to have to find all those 62 birds and see just how snappy these alligators are. Deadass, I'm going to be like that penguin from Werner Herzog's Encounters at the End of the World: The PCG team explained even if they caught me and brought me back to the city, I would immediately head back for the woods.

Refueling my car. I'm not exactly well known for playing GTA games in a *normal* way (if there is such a thing), like I spent most of GTA 5 riding around the backcountry on a dirtbike listening to the radio, and not much time at all actually committing crimes. While I am curious about Leonida's dirtbiking potential, my first port of call is the gas station. Having to refuel your car in a GTA game is such an alien concept I just want to see how the whole process works. How much does it cost? Is there an animation? Do I have to go into the gas station? I'll drive around a little bit first to empty the tank and then that's where I'm heading. I know, I know, I live for thrills.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:.

The original article continues below.

It has been revealed that as initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a newly introduced set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is at the moment known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

This now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

According to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find fresh work soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ENHANCEMENT 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

It has been revealed that latest Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

Industry observers note that there'll be fresh versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker enhancement 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A Latest Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, currently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a Newly introduced Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Upgrade 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The newly introduced game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • To pet animals in GTA 6, you need to approach them and press L2 or LT, which gives you the option to praise them.
  • This is effectively the same as interacting with NPCs, but the option doesn't appear in the bottom of the screen for animals, meaning it's not so clear how to do so.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, knowing whether you can pet animals in GTA 6 should be one of the first questions you ask yourself, as it should in any game with animals in, to be honest. And, as ever, there's loads of wildlife in GTA 6 - though despite how it might sound above, I don't suggest you try and pet the alligators.Dogs and cats, though, can absolutely be played with and, provided you're making an effort to win Lucia back, you may come across one of the cutest cats we've ever seen pretty early on in Chapter 1, though it's not obvious how to interact with them. So, don't get too distracted, but here's how to pet animals in GTA 6.

To pet animals in GTA 6, you need to approach them and press L2 or LT, which gives you the option to praise them. Praise them a few times and you'll finally see the option to pet them, though this doesn't always work.

This is effectively the same as interacting with NPCs, but the option doesn't appear in the bottom of the screen for animals, meaning it's not so clear how to do so. By pressing L2 or LT on an unidentified animal also gives you the option to 'Study' them, which is the only way to add them to your collection of all the GTA 6 animals. You might also see the option to 'Scold' them, but we don't do that. Ever.

It has been revealed that of course you won't be able to pet all animals, just the domesticated ones, but there are different breeds to find, so do make sure you interact with, study, and of course pet every dog and cat you see. The one seen in the images above are of the adorable grocery store employee that you'll find in Key Lento Mini Mart, so go stock up on supplies and meet them while you're at it. In fact, if you're working on improving your GTA 6 relationship status with Lucia, you should pick up some groceries before picking her up from jail. If you've already missed this, good luck making it up to her.

Early on, it was reported that Ellison had considerable faith in Weiss and, per a recent report, she entered the company like a “hero” of sorts. In some circles, Weiss was viewed as a breath of fresh air for CBS News, while other pundits viewed her as something of a wildcard. Nevertheless, given her success with her online platform, The Free Press (which was acquired by the now-defunct Paramount Skydance), she had reason to be confident. According to recent reports, bari arrived like a conquering hero, promising to fix everything. But you can't save a network if nobody is watching. People are asking, 'What exactly are we paying for?'.

Recent findings suggest that the past few months have seen some of CBS News’ programming – like CBS Evening News and 60 Minutes – experience drops in their ratings. Remarked declines in viewership have notably come on the heels of staffing changes made the indicates. For instance, Weiss named Tony Dokoupil as the lead anchor of the evening news program earlier this year, while she and executive producer Nick Bilton fired several high-profile staffers from 60 this past summer.

In a recent development, as noted by Radar, 60 Minutes’ October 11th broadcast notched on 6.06million viewers and, within that sum were 767,000 adults within the aged 25-54 demographic. That number marked a 10 million decrease from the previous week. All the while, CBS Mornings has come in behind morning news shows from rival networks. Following Dokoupil’s debut on CBS Evening News this past March, that show dropped below 4 million viewers, signifying a 15% decrease from the previous year. A network insider added this about the stats:.

In a recent development, these numbers make executives nervous. You can survive bad press and angry employees. But when viewers disappear, everybody wants somebody to blame.

How Bari Weiss Responded After Being Asked If She’d Like To Run CNN.

Weiss herself is aware of the concerns, and she recently addressed the 60 Minutes responses head on, asserting that the show is doing “tremendously well.” The E-I-C also shed light on her biggest goal for CBS News moving forward. Per Weiss, her desire is to build the organization into an institution that the general public can rely on in “an era of collapsing trust.” She also wants to “marry the energy and vibrancy and vitality of the independent creator world” with “the rigor and standards of” a legacy news brand.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, another insider alleges that Bari Weiss is “making enemies inside the building while losing viewers outside it,” which is apparently a “deadly combination.” These allegations should, of course, all be taken with a grain of salt, as CBS News nor parent company Skydance have given any indication that Weiss’ job is in jeopardy. For now, we can only wait and see how she continues to navigate her position.

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

The title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the company wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:.

In a recent development, according to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first unveiled a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

Industry observers note that IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

#39943. Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (470 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (470 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • According to recent reports, the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the firm of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

Recent findings suggest that it's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

Industry observers note that in a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Sources indicate that every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 debuted on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and debuted either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, claims it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

In a recent development, it comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

Industry observers note that with Grand Theft Auto 6âs world being as big as it is and current consoles being six years old, thereâs naturally a bit of worry about how the game performs on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Our reviewer played the game on a PS5 Pro, considered to be the most powerful console on the market right now, and remarked that while it runs at 30 frames-per-second most of the time, there were still some noticeable frame drops in crowded areas.

According to recent reports, but if you havenât bought a PS5 Pro, what can you expect from GTA 6âs performance? Well, the folks over at Digital Foundry have done what they do best and created some lengthy technical breakdowns of the game, including stress testing it in explosive situations.

According to their video, the PS5 Pro tends to hold a pretty solid 30fps, unless you go around making a mess by blowing up a lot of cars at once; in those moments Digital Foundry saw the game dip to around 24fps at its lowest. The base PS5, however, seems to struggle to maintain 30fps in the best of cases, and if you decide to cause a lot of on-screen destruction, those dips are actually sustained until you leave an area.Â.

Industry observers note that on the Xbox side, the Xbox Series X seems to share the same relative stability as the PS5 Pro, with the same frame drops during car chases, crowded scenes, or firefights when things get busier on screen. The big question is how the Xbox Series S, which was originally released in 2020 as a cheaper, lower-powered alternative to the bougie, more expensive consoles of the year, handles GTA 6. According to Digital Foundry, there are some details that are less prevalent or rendered with lower-res textures, and the resolution is lower, coming in at 720p compared to the 1440p of Series X.

The DF video has a number of comparison shots demonstrating how a lot of small details have been downgraded on Series S, but the real difference is that the framerate is, unsurprisingly, struggling the most on the less powerful Xbox. Digital Foundry reports that while 30fps is the target, even the most “typical” play can affect framerate, with standard combat encounters and car chases dropping it to around 25 and the more demanding carnage bringing it down to 20. There’s even a few seconds in the video where it gets down to 18 and 19fps during an explosive shootout.

Ultimately, if youâre hoping for the smoothest possible experience, the PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X are the unsurprising winners here. A PC version of the game is rumored to launch sometime next year, and I imagine thatâs where folks with high-end builds are going to be able to get smoother, 60fps framerates as Rockstar apparently has no plans to add a Performance Mode to GTA6 on consoles. If youâre running a Series S, maybe try not to cause too much mayhem along the way for best results.Â.

Sources indicate that upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

Industry observers note that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a manufacturer succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development problems, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg remarked it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • At an awards screening attended by GamesRadar+, JD Payne, who created the show with Patrick McKay, contextualizes Sauron's mission to craft the One Ring.
  • In a recent development, payne goes on to explain that Galadriel plays a part in this for Sauron too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Rings of Power season 3 has been building up to Sauron's forging of the One Ring for a while now, and it's finally due to debut in episode 7. However, one of the showrunners has confirmed that it's not just a tactical move for the Dark Lord, but a personal one too.

At an awards screening attended by GamesRadar+, JD Payne, who created the show with Patrick McKay, contextualizes Sauron's mission to craft the One Ring. "We flash forward five years from the end of season two, and he's already taken over lots of Middle-earth," he explains. "His armies have conquered many things, but he can't conquer the two Elven realms because of the three Elven rings that are protecting them. And so, forging the One Ring is going to be the key towards him finally getting what he wants, and really this season is about exploring what that means for him.".

In a recent development, payne goes on to explain that Galadriel plays a part in this for Sauron too. "We always knew he wanted to conquer and be able to rule the three Elven rings, the seven Dwarven rings, the nine rings for Men. But this season, you have to understand a little bit more about what that means from a character point of view.".

"That conquering the Elven rings isn't just about an abstract political goal, but there's a personal part of it as well," he adds. "As Celebrimbor taunts him early on and notes that without the One Ring, he'll never be capable of mastering her, speaking of Galadriel, and that's a relationship we spent two years really building up.".

Industry observers note that the moment Payne is referencing comes in season 3's opening episode, 'Marnûkh'. After another failed attempt at forging the ring, Celebrimbor visits Sauron in a vision. "You took part in the forging of the Seven, and of the Nine, but the Three you had no hand in," he states. "Without knowing their secrets you will never create a ring capable of mastering them, of mastering her. How does that feel, knowing that the conquests that you so desire will forever elude your grasp?".

It certainly seems that everything really boils down to Galadriel for Sauron, which is something that Charlie Vickers teased to GamesRadar+ ahead of season 3. He told us Sauron is "frustrated" because Galadriel remains "beyond his reach".

For more on the upcoming One Ring sequence, take a look at our exclusive deep dive into the "most complex" thing the show has ever done.

Industry observers note that the Rings of Power season 3 has two episodes remaining. Make sure you don't miss anything with our The Rings of Power season 3 release schedule and check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review for why you should be watching.

As far as fashion goes, trends can fluctuate as time goes on and, in many cases, celebrities are at the forefront of such crazes. One particular trend that seems to have taken hold of Hollywood as of late involves the little black dress, as more than a few actresses have donned it. And more specifically, many have been going for that sheer, lacy style when taking on the look. Even Alexandria Daddario has worn a LBD in the last few months but, more recently, the actress dazzled by switching things up with a gold outfit.

Daddario is in the midst of promoting her 2026 movie schedule, Hershey, and she recently hit her first premiere for the film, which was held in Hershey, Pennsylvania at the Hershey Theater. For the event, Daddario – who plays Catherine "Kitty" Hershey in the movie – wore the draping, gold dress that shimmered. And, even when she wasn’t actually on the red carpet, the actress posed in the ensemble while taking a selfie in front of a mirror. Take a look at the sweet outfit in the Instagram post below:.

A post shared by alexandra daddario (@alexandradaddario).

This particular outfit feels appropriate for a few reasons, one of which is the fact that Daddario is known for sporting shinier ensembles. I’m specifically thinking back to the time that she wore that Oscar De La Renta dress to a Tag Heuer event back in 2023. That look included some particularly sweet-looking, silver sequins. While this gold dress (for which Daddario didn’t identify a designer) is less grandiose, it’s still more than effective and makes a classy statement.

According to recent reports, another reason why this outfit is fitting (no pun intended) for such a premiere is that it almost feels like a homage to Hershey’s gold products, which have since been discontinued. Of course, I’m definitely not sure if that’s what Daddario and her stylist were going for when picking that dress. However, I still find it to be a happy coincidence, and I can’t help but wonder if I’m the only one who has made that connection.

But, as previously mentioned, Alexandra Daddario’s outfit really does feel like a breath of fresh air during a time at which the black dress trend seems to be taking over in a big way. That’s not to say those outfits haven’t been impressive, mind you. Back in September, Jennifer Lopez wore a black, Dolce & Gabbana dress, which she paired with a fur coat. And, more recently, McKenna Grace married the sheer and black dress trends when wearing a mini dress from Annie's Ibiza.

Industry observers note that I also have to shout out Florence Pugh, who hasn’t exactly gone sheer with the LBD craze but has been finding interesting ways to shake it up a bit amid her press tour for East of Eden. During a FYC event, she recently wore a black dress from Harris Reed’s spring 2027 collection, which had sleeves that could only be compared to Mickey Mouse ears. (And that last comment is meant to be complimentary.) She went ruffle-free at the Jaguar Type 01 Reveal, though, as she wore a svelte, black dress that she paired with a silver necklace.

It has been revealed that yes, the fashionistas are indeed out and about, and they’re definitely dressed to impress. Chances are we’ll be seeing more stunning looks from Daddario and more as awards season progresses and film premieres continue to crop up. In the meantime, I’m just curious as to how Daddario might follow up this sultry, gold piece.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that iâve been playing Barbie Rewind in bits and odd pieces.
  • I like the idea of Barbie Rewind, and Iâm glad these games are available again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in the waning hours before GTA VI becomes available on my living room console, I am (for now) posted up at my PC, blasting bright, neon pink directly into my retinas. Just like when I was a kid.

Sources indicate that iâve been playing Barbie Rewind in bits and odd pieces. Released last week, itâs another retro game collection from Digital Eclipse that thankfully makes 16 classics playable again for normal people who donât have giant retro console collections, decades after their original releases. One of those gamesâBarbie: Vacation Adventureânever even got a full release until now, and was previously only known via a handful of magazine previews. Now, you can play it.

I like the idea of Barbie Rewind, and Iâm glad these games are available again. But the presentation of this collection leaves a lot wanting. Itâs buggy, for oneâI had weird audio blips in both the Dreamhouse segments (more on those in a moment) and in several of the games, with sound and music cutting out randomly or going fuzzy like a radio. Barbie Super Sports was, I hate to use the phrase but, literally unplayableâonce I got to the skiing section, I couldnât move my character at all in any direction no matter how many times I tried or what buttons I pushed. At one point, I spent so long navigating back and forth in and out of menus trying to check the controls that my menu got stuck on the controls page, leaving me unable to exit the game without hard shutting it down. Unfortunately, doing so erased all of my progress in both Super Sports and two other games I had tried prior, which in turn set me back on my objectives in the Dreamhouse. I also just found most of the games difficult to parse visually in their original resolution on a modern 1080p monitor; surely something should have been done about that?

It has been revealed that for that reason, I find the Dreamhouse bit of Barbie Rewind far more compelling than the games that are the actual purpose of the collection. As you play the retro games, you unlock upcoming rooms in a Dreamhouse and new furniture to fill them with. The decor is all taken from Barbie playsets over the years: couches, tables, lamps, phones, beds, and so forth. While the decorating mechanics are pretty simple, the decorations themselves are bright and colorful neons and pastels in funky and often retro shapes and styles, daring you to try to make them fit an orderly theme. Just as I would want a pile of mixed-up playsets to be.

I imagine that those who played with such things growing up will recognize them, but itâs reminded me that despite being a Barbie fiend, I never had any Barbie playsets growing up. Just dolls and clothes. I would build houses for them out of a couple of empty KâNEX boxes, or use the couch and pillows to make small Barbie forts. Iâm a little jealous of whoever got to mess around with all this plastic, though Iâm sure that, had I had any of this, it would have gotten lost like all the little Barbie shoes that disappeared over the years. Itâs not the same, decorating a virtual Dreamhouse. But itâs a nice enough approximation, given that Iâm not about to go out and buy any of this in reality.

Rachel Simone Weil, a girls video game and toy historian, played a major role in getting the Dreamhouse aspects together. She served as a historical consultant on Barbie Rewind, and especially focused on making sure the Dreamhouse elements were an accurate and celebratory portrayal of Barbie history. Obviously, Barbie Rewind could not include every single playset ever made, so Weil had to be selective as she tapped into different aspects of Barbie history. What were the most crucial relics of Barbie history?

âObviously, the iconic playsets, the ones that fans remember, those really tactile memories of just the feeling of the plastic or the way the box smelled,â she remarked. âThere are certain playsets, I think, that are really emblematic of the brand. I think of the Beach Blast pool. That’s pretty iconic. Obviously, the original Barbie Dreamhouse. We also included some deep cuts. There’s Cafe Today, which is pretty rare and hard to come by, especially in good condition, but a beautiful, psychedelic-designed cafe.â.

In addition to the mix of iconic sets and deep cuts, Weil also wanted to emphasize technology, given the video game-ness of Barbie Rewind. And Barbie has quite the technological history. Weil tells me about playsets from before I was born making a point to include computers, phones, record players, CD players, and so forth. Barbie was always hip, always on top of the latest trends both in fashion and in tech.

âThe Barbie Dreamhouse from 1979 has this nightstand with this little tiny computer in it,â Weil indicates. Iâve seen it, I have it in my Barbie Rewind Dreamhouse right now, and it looks wonderfully retro and ridiculous. âAnd in â79, personal computers were just starting to come out. So, you’re starting to see people imagining what computers might be, right? And then you see Day to Night Barbie in the â80s, you start to see the IBM PC style playset computers.

It has been revealed that âOh, another one I really like is the travel agent playset from, I think, 1986. The travel industry was famously one of the first industries to adopt computer technology. And right as it’s happening, Barbie is there with that travel agent playset and she’s got a computer. And the home office playsets from the â80s and â90s. Barbie’s got a home computer. She goes to work and she does computers.â.

Barbie was a massive, massive part of my childhood. For a solid eight, nine, ten years, Barbie was one of my predominant interests. Dressing up those dolls, taking them to friendsâ houses, and playing make-believe was formative for me, and two of the video games in this collection (Barbie Super Sports and Barbie Race and Ride) represent my earliest memories of playing video games at all. I was playing Barbie long before I had my hands on Mario or Zelda.

Sources indicate that and yet, Barbie is rarely if ever considered to be on equal footing with those classics. In some ways, I get itâmainstream gaming is bent far more toward the kinds of games that Mario and Zelda evolved to become. And yet, Infinity Nikki is massive. So is The Sims. The Style Savvy series on Nintendo handhelds was super popular, as were animal-focused games like Nintendogs. Heck, we just heard everyone praising Dressmaker. These games have always been with us, and Barbie pioneered a lot of what they would become. Itâs unfortunately not too hard to work out why Barbie doesnât get the respect she deserves.

Recent findings suggest that âBarbie Rewind is the first retro game compilation that centers predominantly girl-led experiences in console gaming, right, of the 20th century,â Weil says. âThese games were a significant deal when they came out in terms of popularity, sales, and it’s not just about the market impact. These games had a big, like, left a big impression on the people that played them, right?

Sources indicate that âGirls who played these games in the â80s, â90s, â00s are adults now, and they’re looking back on these games with fondness and nostalgia and stories about, you know, negotiating with their siblings about who got the controller and the hours poured into them. There’s really not beenâI’d say there’s been a lack of an outlet for that fondness or way to revisit these games or even an acknowledgement from the world that these Barbie games, they weren’t just a fever dream, not only were they real, but we can play them again on modern platforms. So, I think for Digital Eclipse and Atari to put out this collection in collaboration with Mattel, I think it’s really gratifying, a gratifying acknowledgement that women’s retro gaming experiences are valid, vital, and they’re part of the broader retro gaming culture at large, and they deserve to be included.â.

According to recent reports, itâs not just girls, either. David Lowey, director of marketing at Atari, is here to champion girl games for everyone. âIt’s amazing how many people I’ve spoken to, particularly guys I’ve spoken to, who have played a significant amount of these games. And the answer is always the same. It was like, âYeah, it was on the PC in the kitchen. It was my sister’s game, but I played the hell out of it.â I heard that so much.â.

Recently, an interview with the developers of Dressmaker sparked some social media discussion around women as gamers, and whether they are being adequately served by games that reflect their interests. Itâs a tricky discussion. On one hand, itâs obviously narrow-minded to assume that women are only going to be interested in games about fashion and vacation and pet rescue and horses. But on the other, it is true that many women do find those things interesting, and that because those things are typically associated with women, games like the ones in Barbie Rewind are less common and often not as well-funded or supported as more âmasculineâ games.

Weil had not seen the Dressmaker discourse when I spoke to her and thus didnât want to comment on the interview specifically, but I asked her to tell me more broadly: what are we talking about when we talk about Girl Games? What does it mean for a game to be a Girl Game?

âFirst of all, it’s changed a lot in the last 15 years,â she states. âI think 15 years ago it was very difficult to have that conversation. I remember being in grad school and having professors say, âyou can’t study Barbie video games.â I remember having an exhibit vandalized. People were upset about the idea that we would talk about girlsâ video games, or that acknowledging that they existed and celebrating those memories was the same as saying, âgirls must do this, and girls must love pink and whatever.â And so it’s a difficult conversation.â.

Weil goes on to say that she intentionally uses the phrase âgirl gameâ to provoke that difficult conversation: to get people talking about the dichotomy between what girls must be, what they can be, and what theyâre allowed to be.

Industry observers note that âOne thing that I think about as a historian is that this scrutiny of girl games, [where people ask], âIs this set modeling the right behaviors for girls? Is this setting up the right expectations for what femininity means and all this stuff?â We’re not asking those same questions about boy games. We’re not asking, is Mega Man a good role model for boys? Is Mega Man going to teach boys to, you know, be this or that? Or, if we’re asking those questions, it’s not preventing Mega Man from being part of retro gaming canon, right?

âFor me as a historian, I’m not saying we shouldn’t ask those questions, or we shouldn’t talk about those social problems. But I think we have a tendency to let the pendulum swing too far and say, âthere are social issues around this. And so let’s put all the Barbie games in the trash.â We can’t do that. I think the history of girlsâ video games has been forgotten and rediscovered like three or four times because this behavior of saying, âThis is a delicate subject, this touches on social topics or discrimination or stereotypes or things like that. And I feel nervous about that. And so I’m just going to pretend that these games didn’t exist.â We can’t do that.â.

Mattel is looking to succeed where Hasbro failed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a upcoming Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to recent reports, according to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three latest projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources noted it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas debuted in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two upcoming Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

#39933. Tech Report: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

Tech Report: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Sources indicate that it wasn't ever thus.
  • It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

Sources indicate that it wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross New York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

It has been revealed that the pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something fresh," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty rapidly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

In a recent development, the increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Sources indicate that rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

Sources indicate that while never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

It has been revealed that as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij stated, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

According to recent reports, needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

Industry observers note that according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

Sources indicate that "I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

It has been revealed that "At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".
