📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you hear the name Lil’ Kim, a variety of images come to mind. She’s forever known as the force of nature from Brooklyn who turned the music industry on its head when she entered the scene, and her bodacious lyrics and unique fashion sense have kept her as a source of inspiration on your favorite designer’s mood board ever since. On November 18 and 19, to celebrate the music that cemented her icon status, Lil’ Kim will perform in front of a symphony orchestra at the Kings Theatre in Brooklyn, not far from her humble beginnings.

Recent findings suggest that today she’s less interested in being in the spotlight and more focused on raising her 12-year-old daughter, Royal Reign. In between practices for her performances, Lil’ Kim spoke with Vanity Fair to reflect on her career, how she spends her days, and her standout looks.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: What do you remember about putting your debut album, Hard Core, together?

It has been revealed that lil’ Kim: I remember Biggie and Un [Lance Rivera], who was the label owner that we had. I watched Un build a record label called Undeas, which [stood] for “Un ideas,” and then he finally sold it to Atlantic Records. At the time, we didn’t know the process, but we became Undeas-Atlantic. I remember Biggie having the idea of how he wanted my album to be red, and he explained it to me and Un. I was able to write according to how his idea was to present me, because when they met me, I was who I was—in high heels, jeans, motorcycle jackets, and furs at 13.

Portrait of members of R&B group 112 and rappers Notorious MASSIVE and Lil’ Kim circa 1996.

That’s incredible. It sounds like your fashion-icon status started very early. Was there anyone that you looked to back then? What inspired you to dress that way?

Recent findings suggest that my mom was a big inspiration to me when it came to fashion, and so I looked to her for a lot of things. I used to wear her mink coat. She used to wear big sunglasses with her fur coats, with the diamonds and jewelry. She was always taking vacations and I would see her pack her stuff, and she would always have the cutest outfits. They were all matchy-matchy. It’s funny because she would have her outfit to go play tennis in and her outfit would match her tennis racket. So when I bought my big house, I bought a Chanel tennis outfit and I bought the racket to match it, because of my mom.

In a recent development, I love that. Do you keep up with tennis or specifically the ladies in tennis?

No, I haven’t in a while, but, of course, you know, Serena and Venus were like my heroes.

Well, maybe we need to see you on the court one day.

I know. I’m pretty sure I’m rusty, but I like to get out there, though. I used to beat my cousin’s butt back then.

How did the symphony performances come about?

Sources indicate that my agents called me and they’re like, “Kim, what do you think?” And I was like, “That’s a freaking awesome idea.” I love performing with bands. And so I imagine that it could be very similar, if not very close. And I thought this could be something really different for me. Sometimes I even listen to classical music. I don’t have to know who the artist is, but I just put on a station and let it flow.

Do you have a favorite song from Hard Core?

Recent findings suggest that I love “Queen Bitch”; it’s my favorite song. It’s still my favorite to perform. And “Crush on You.”.

Salma Hayek, Donatella Versace, Pamela Anderson, and Lil’ Kim at Versace’s spring/summer 2001 fashion show.

When it comes to fashion, you’re obviously on everyone’s mood board, from stylists to designers, so how vital was fashion for you as part of the Lil’ Kim persona?

I just was being myself, honestly. When I first met Biggie, I was coming from my after-school job at Bloomingdale’s. I was probably 13 or 14 at the time, and they would let the teenagers work there.

But I had on a motorcycle jacket and high heels. And one of my best friends told Biggie, “You know, my girl can rap,” because we knew he was rapping around the way. And he was like, “I heard you can rap.” And I just laughed. He was like, “Yeah, see, I knew you didn’t know how to rap.” He was very condescending. He knew how to get you to do what you wanted to do, because I was really shy.

Sources indicate that and then I started rapping, and he was blown away because I had on high heels. No one had ever seen someone just bust a rap in high heels. When Biggie, Un, and Jacob York started really talking to me, they didn’t want to change me because that was just what they were so blown away about. That was just who I was.

Do you think people ever misunderstood the way you presented yourself?

Industry observers note that to be honest, I never really felt misunderstood by my hardcore fans—the kids my age and the younger kids, they totally got it. I think that’s why I had such a cult following and there was such pandemonium about me when I came out. They understood me. I think it was the older people and the politicians, those are the people who I think misunderstood me.

What did you think of the midterm elections and all of the women who broke barriers in the Senate and gubernatorial offices?

I’m going to be honest with you, I stay away from politics.

Are you keeping up with all of the changes within fashion today? When I listen to your music, you’ve mentioned so many designers and houses, and since then the creative directors have changed. Are you following all of the changes within fashion and seeing how you’re still a part of the conversation?

According to recent reports, that’s what I’m trying to say. As a fashion icon, if you really her, and I’m considering myself really her, that’s never gonna change. That’s never going to change. I might put on a fur coat that my stylist or myself will get asked about, because I style myself a lot. And I was styling myself then.

Lil’ Kim and daughter, Royal Reign, on June 16, 2016, in New York City.

What has motherhood been like for you?

Recent findings suggest that extremely rewarding. My daughter’s with me all the time. This world is so cruel and so evil; it’s so different. She’s my safe haven. I feel the extra need to keep her safe.

What does a regular day look like for you?

Lately, I’ve just been really getting into myself. I get up and go have a little spa day. I might take my daughter to go do whatever she wants.

Singer Mary J. Blige with Diana Ross and Lil’ Kim at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards on September 9, 1999.

How do you feel that we’re still talking about your MTV VMAs look in 1999?

I think it’s iconic and I love it. I love when they bring that up, because it was a fun day and it was so good to see people’s faces when they saw my outfit.

Are there any other looks that don’t get as much love as you wish that they did?

Industry observers note that I don’t know, because most of the looks that I love, they get the love. There’s a look when I was on the cover of Nylon magazine and I had the teddy bear dress on; that’s one of my favorite looks. The Louis Vuitton look is one of my favorite looks; I love that look. A lot of the Chanel looks and the Versace and the Chanel in the hair.

Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, one million copies for each month on sale, it seems.
  • That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.
  • Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It promptly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen mentioned.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a new character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active people to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

Recent findings suggest that "Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours.".

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

Looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be unveiled, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart new additions build on what made the original work so well.

#39780. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1130 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity.
  • Recent findings suggest that when you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S.
  • According to recent reports, if you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

Recent findings suggest that when you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

According to recent reports, if you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

It has been revealed that IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create concerns. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

WebRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

But the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Sources indicate that even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

According to recent reports, if you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Recent findings suggest that websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Recent findings suggest that even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

In a recent development, VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

Recent findings suggest that while this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

It has been revealed that before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS matter, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:.

We’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

It has been revealed that in case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

There’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty major bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

In a recent development, "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a latest generation of video game narrative designers.

According to recent reports, "One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.".

Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV indicates and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

Cash is king in GTA 6, and Rockstar has come up with some new systems to manage your finances, from a secret stash under the floorboards to an honest-to-goodness interest-bearing savings account.

Recent findings suggest that but you need to be careful with your money, especially at the start of the game when even a few hundred bucks can make or break you. While wandering around Leonida, strangers might try to rob you (big mistake), but more importantly, if you die or get arrested, you'll be penalized a few hundred dollars. There's also a $20k limit to how much you can keep on your person as you gradually accumulate more and more through play.

Recent findings suggest that the solution? Stash your cash frequently. During the initial chapters of the game, you won't have a bank account, but you can store your money in your house in Key Lento by simply stashing it under the floorboards in the bedroom. This will mean you have a little money tucked away, and won't lose it when you die or get busted by the cops. .

Remember, you can also stash stolen goods like jewelry, drugs, and marked bills from robberies in the trunk of your car. Even if your car gets impounded by the fuzz, you'll be able to recover that contraband from your trunk later on and sell it. Don't stash goods in a car you don't own, though: you might lose it if you lose that car.

Sources indicate that here's the crucial bit of advice: you might be tempted to deposit all your cash, but if you do, you'll miss out on a variety of real-time and random opportunities in the game. There are a bunch of street encounters in GTA 6 reliant on you having some cash in your pocket, such as the time a stranger promised to tell me a secret in exchange for a few dollars—and then offered me more secrets for even more money, and then teased me with the biggest secret of all for more cash than I had on me. I'm still wondering what that final secret was!

Sometimes you'll have the opportunity to bribe someone for quick access to a restricted area, or you'll meet a pool hustler in a dive bar and want to pony up cash for a quick game. GTA 6's living city and its random occurrences are part of the attraction of the game, after all. There are a few vendors that only take cash, too. The point is, when you're making your deposits, always hold back a few hundred for your wallet.

In a recent development, when you reach the mission called "Buck Me" in Chapter 1 you'll unlock a bank account, which will more easily let you deposit your cash in nearby ATMs. You can spot these on the map by the hand with the credit card symbol—just walk up to one and interact with it to dump your cash. Having an account will also unlock certain weapons for purchase.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Sources indicate that the Buck Me app on your phone also lets you "Buck Yourself"—transfer money into a joint savings account Jason and Lucia share. Any money you put into that savings account can't be withdrawn, so while it's good to sock away funds for the future, keep in mind you're shutting yourself off from your own money.

No matter how responsible (or irresponsible) you are with your cashflow, always remember to keep a few hundred in your wallet. If one of GTA 6's cash-based encounters happens, the last thing you want to do is have to run off and look for the nearest ATM.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the tech giant created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the company's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

"Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

"The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.".

In a recent development, this tallies with the narrative spun by co-firm leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard said.

The situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "major American company" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

Sources indicate that it had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it launched, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was confirmed in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that according to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025.
  • Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the latest storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

Industry observers note that according to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

The easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

It has been revealed that reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

According to recent reports, sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are presently on a hijacked browsing session.

Industry observers note that change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

In a recent development, look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

Grab your bell bottoms and cowboy hats — because Lainey Wilson kicked up some dust and brought the country charm in her 2026 CMA Awards opening monologue with some assistance from none other than legend and bonafide #Swiftie, Brad Paisley.

As Wilson, 34, kicked off the Wednesday, November 18, ceremony at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Paisley, 54, crashed the party to rewrite several of the biggest country hits of all time with updated lyrics.

“This is bigger than me: We have to talk about the biggest story of the year. Somebody got married,” Paisley exclaimed, revealing the bride was a “blonde singer” who married a “football player.” (Taylor Swift, of course, married Travis Kelce in July just months after Wilson tied the know with Devlin “Duck” Hodges.).

“It was such a big deal,” Paisley added before Wilson thanked her fellow singer for mentioning her big day.

“You got married? What arena did you get married in?” Paisley added, referring to Swift’s Madison Square Garden wedding venue. Wilson and Hodges, however, noted “I do” inside a cave.

“I will never forget what my husband remarked to me when we went looking for wedding venues,” Wilson said, setting up another original song. “I beg your pardon/ I never promised Madison Square Garden.”.

The cameras cut to Swift, 36, who laughed alongside BFF Brittany Mahomes, who is married to Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs teammate Patrick Mahomes.

According to recent reports, “I can’t believe I wasn’t invited to your wedding,” Paisley added. “I did go to Taylor’s. Hi, Taylor! Remember me? I ate all the shrimp.”.

Wednesday’s ceremony is Wilson’s third time emceeing Country’s Biggest Night, made even more special considering her three nominations. Wilson is up for Entertainer of the Year, Single of the Year and Female Vocalist of the Year.

It has been revealed that “I am gathering ideas and I’ll tell you one of my ideas because I told Ella [Langley] this,” she teased on an episode of Country Heat Weekly last month, referring to Langley’s nine nods. “I stated, ‘Girl, I’m going to bring you a bedazzled broom,’ so she can sweep it up. I’m going to be there with a bedazzled dust pan.”.

Jokes aside, Wilson knows that attending — and earning CMA trophies — is a huge honor in itself.

In a recent development, “I think it just stands for representing country as a genre, whatever that looks like,” she added on the podcast. “Each year that I have been nominated for Entertainer of the Year, I feel like it looks like something different for me. I think it just means representing the genre in the best light that you possibly can. And there’s a lot of people doing that.”.

Wilson’s 2023 Entertainer of the Year accolade represented the first time a woman won the category in a decade. (She took home the trophy for the second time during the 2025 awards show.).

In a recent development, “I’ve known since I moved to Nashville in 2011 that there are going to be some barn doors I was going to have to go kick down myself, that nobody was going to do it [for me],” Wilson exclusively told Us in November 2025 of breaking through the industry’s glass ceiling. “It was truly a bitter pill that I swallowed a long time ago. So in the times when I felt like maybe it’s a little bit harder just because I’m a girl, that’s when I dug in deeper and worked harder.”.

Since she found success, Wilson has tried to help mentor other rising artists.

“Being a listening ear, sharing the wisdom that was passed along to me from people like Reba [McEntire] and Dolly [Parton], who were more than willing to give me that wisdom from the goodness of their heart,” she recalled. “Everything they say, I bottle it up. Industry News: Stacey Abrams in Conversation With Ta-Nehisi Coates

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4125 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when I first met Stacey Abrams in 2015, she passed on to me the message that she was then passing on to anyone who’d listen: Someday soon, Georgia would be blue.
  • The following conversation has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
  • Ta-Nehisi Coates: My recollection of our first meeting goes back to 2015, when I was promoting Between the World and Me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when I first met Stacey Abrams in 2015, she passed on to me the message that she was then passing on to anyone who’d listen: Someday soon, Georgia would be blue. This struck me as unlikely. But three years later Abrams ran for governor, and shocked the country by coming within two points of winning. Then two years later, when Joe Biden sealed his presidential election in 2020 with a win in Georgia, and Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff won Senate seats, Abrams looked prophetic. Now, Democrats have gone beyond Georgia, penetrating into the deepest reaches of the South—Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas. To understand how the GOP’s Solid South grew brittle, I could think of no better person to talk to than Abrams.

The following conversation has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Ta-Nehisi Coates: My recollection of our first meeting goes back to 2015, when I was promoting Between the World and Me. You interviewed me for the book. We had a wonderful discussion. My family was actually in the audience, because, like all Black folks, I have family in Atlanta. They were so excited. I was talking to Stacey Abrams—Minority Leader Stacey Abrams. And one of the things you said backstage was, “We’re going to make Georgia blue.” And I don’t know that I scoffed at you. I like to think I wasn’t quite that rude.

Stacey Abrams: Your eyebrow arched a bit.

I confess to the eyebrow arching. And so the eyebrow arched and you made the case. Can you tell me what you saw?

It has been revealed that I’d gone through redistricting, and one of the component pieces of redistricting, of course, is that it’s predicated on the census. The US census is a tool that is incredibly powerful and deeply inexact. It was the first time Republicans had power to draw the lines since Reconstruction. And I took a posture in my caucus, and it was this: “If you vote for their maps, I will come after your seats.” And I was not only unequivocal in saying it, I wrote it down because I didn’t want anyone to misquote me.

In a recent development, in order to take that posture, I had to read the maps myself. And what I saw was that Republicans were placing bets that, by drawing the lines a certain way, they were going to give themselves 124 of 180 seats. So 67% of the seats, even though they’d only won the election by 57%.

Recent findings suggest that but I looked at those same maps and I’m like, In this place, in this part of Paulding County, there is a new subdivision that is predominantly Black. And in this part of Gwinnett County, there is a burgeoning Korean population that is now going into its second generation, which means a lot of those will be eligible voters. And down in South Georgia, you have third-generation migrant farm workers who are Latino, but who have decided to plant their roots here and raise their families here. When you looked at those numbers, the maps had a very different story to tell about Republican dominance: They could win for a decade. They could not win for a generation.

Sources indicate that we tell ourselves stories about the information we get, and people repeat stories without ever reading it themselves. There are a lot of people who can quote Tom Sawyer who’ve never read the book. And so in our politics, that happens a lot, that the story that becomes popular doesn’t ever get traced back to its origin or to the original text.

What I saw in Georgia is true in Louisiana, in Mississippi, in Tennessee, in Alabama, in South Carolina. We just saw it happen in North Carolina.

So when you saw this wave of redistricting happening around the country this year, did you see a similar opportunity?

Oh, absolutely. I was in Tennessee the day that they passed the maps and what stuck out for me was Raumesh Akbari, who’s the Senate minority leader, she asked to see the bill, and the Republican chair of the committee stated, “Well, we don’t have a bill yet, but we know what it’s going to say.” They planned to vote on it even though they did not have the text of the bill.

Recent findings suggest that the Republicans were moving so fast because they thought they understood what they were pulling together. Justin Pearson didn’t pick up the seat he wanted, but they were at risk of losing a seat they thought was going to be theirs because they misread the topography, but they didn’t do a deeper dive into exactly what was laying in the crevices. And that’s where opportunity for us is born.

There are not enough Black people to win any single seat outright on their own in most legislative districts, and no statewide elections, especially post–Louisiana v. Callais, but there are coalitions that can be built. And what I saw from the very beginning was the possibility of coalition.

What I see for the South, what I think the South proved on Tuesday, is the possibility of coalition, but coalition does not happen without conflict. It does not happen without conversation, and it does not happen when we have convinced ourselves of the permanence of our second-class citizenship and our subjugation. What we saw on Tuesday was a moment where people realized that the power to improve their own lives had become so desperately thin that they had to use it or lose it. We cannot rely on that for the next two years.

What I hear you saying is that the last two years created an emergency. But that can’t be depended on. It can’t be “The Most Vital Election of Our Lifetime” every two years. Desperation is not enough.

It can’t be. Desperation gets you one moment. There’s a whole body of medical research on people that have heart attacks and they get saved. And what it demonstrates is that they are exercise fiends for about six weeks and then they fall back into their patterns because it’s a normalcy bias.

If we constantly feel on the edge of danger, we cannot function. And so we reorient our understanding of normal to survive. And therefore our responsibility in this moment is to look at the opportunity that was revealed on Tuesday, but not read into it that that opportunity either requires desperation or it requires this milquetoast approach, because our default is not just normalcy, but the most banal form of normalcy we can imagine.

I know you have some concerns about some of the narratives emerging out of the midterms. Would you talk a bit about that?

I saw something on Axios that I think was well-intentioned and it essentially noted that the threats to our democracy were overblown, that our courts held, that our Congress held, that our presidency wasn’t overreaching, and that for normal people, things were fine. How have we reached the place where we think it is normal that the capital city in the United States of America is under military occupation? How is it okay that the courts held when it permits the incarceration of children in Dilley, Texas, and the kidnapping of people of color because of race and the language that they speak? There is something aggressively privileged about this idea that democracy is not in jeopardy because those who are the most protected don’t feel harm.

But Tuesday was a repudiation of this idea that things are normal. You saw turnout at extraordinary levels from a cross section of communities, almost all of whom have been directly impacted by the harms of this administration. Not just the economic harms that hit everyone, but harms that were amplified and refined for their cruelty.

Industry observers note that at the same time, there’s a worry that I have that, because we won control of Congress for the patriots—and that’s how I frame it, I no longer think it’s just Democrat versus Republican, it’s patriots versus authoritarians—even though the patriots may have gained more purchase in Congress, we still have a Supreme Court that gutted the last vestiges of protection for the Voting Rights Act. We still have a Supreme Court that stripped women of their bodily autonomy. We still have a Supreme Court that has mentioned that protections that are afforded by DEI are somehow suspect. And when those are true, then the successes of Tuesday don’t signal that we’ve won. They signal that we have to work even harder because the harms have not dissipated, they just haven’t penetrated.

You remarked something a few months back that’s stuck with me—that our elections are ripe for entertainment. As a sports fan, I think it’s not a coincidence that so many sports figures are now commenting on politics because the way they appear on TV is actually quite similar to the way sports appears. You have these long campaigns, which is like your season. Then you have primaries, which are like your playoffs, and then you have this significant Super Bowl that happens on Tuesday. And so, it’s an entertainment and ratings bonanza. And I think, as I recall, you were cautioning against that as a view of politics. Can you speak a little bit more about that?

Recent findings suggest that yeah. When you think about politics, if you think about elections as an event, and to extend your analogy, if the elections are the finals, if the elections are game seven, if it’s the Super Bowl, when that happens, then the day after, you go home, the game is over. But the challenge I have is that it’s not just that we treat it as a sporting event, it’s that we treat politics as though we are spectators at a sporting event. And when we look at the other party, it’s like we are spectators watching a very disciplined, seasoned team that practices in the off-season, that travels together, that plays overseas. They’re constantly engaged and we are on and off. We think of politics, again, as entertainment as opposed to the job.

How did we end up with this entertainment narrative?

Industry observers note that theodore White did this series where he examined elections 1960, 1964, 1968, 1972. And when you read it, as someone who is reading it in the 21st century, the arc of how we have viewed politics changed dramatically, specifically in 1960 with the advent of television, because the election contest between John Kennedy and Richard Nixon hinged in no small part on that televised debate. And I think for you and me and for anyone who wasn’t old enough to see it, I did not realize that it was one of the most watched programs in American history. We take for granted how many people are going to watch the debates these days, but with that first debate, it was one of the most watched programs in the world because it had never happened before. And the moment it became a television spectacle, it became entertainment because you were watching, you picked winners and losers, you picked your villain and you picked your champion.

In a recent development, it’s human nature, we put things into these narrative arcs. As someone who writes comic books, you understand this. As someone who writes thrillers, I think about this. You create a villain, you have a protagonist, an antagonist, you have to have a storyline, you have to have complications, and when television became the medium, it added a layer and a texture to what had long been the mechanics of politics. Then you add into it the drama of Black and brown people getting to participate. And then you layer on top of that “blue state versus red state,” and the sharp division, and the attribution to entire regions of a value system and a personality based on a single day.

What would it mean to remain engaged beyond elections? When I think about the conservative movement, I think about the degree to which the religious right is engaged. I think about Trump rallies. I think people were baffled by this at first—the clothes, the trucks, the boats. But what I would say is those are markers of community. They aren’t my politics. But they seem part of something larger than a particular bill or policy.

It has been revealed that there’s a lot of talk in organizing about going for belief first, or belonging first. On the left, we are often accused of belief, that you have to be in line with all of our ideas, our values, our ideologies, but also the tactical, practical ways of exercising them, and that because we say you have to believe first, we filter out people who haven’t had time to understand or adapt or even decide what they believe. The right uses belonging. They say, “Come and be a part of us, and we’ll tell you what we are.” So you get the jersey, you get the cap, you get the red, you get to use the language, even if you haven’t decided that you actually believe all they believe, which is why you have people who are suddenly surprised that this is what happened.

Industry observers note that we have to shift. Not to say that we don’t have beliefs, but we have to give people time to grow into those beliefs. I come at this from my time as minority leader. I had a caucus of 60 members in a chamber of 180, and my members included suburban white mothers and rural Black pastors and everything in between. We were the most racially diverse caucus. We were geographically diverse. And I had no power. I was the minority leader. My job was to help harmonize their approach. I could not lead with belief, because people were entitled to their beliefs, but my job was to bring them into belonging first because they were members of the caucus. And then my second job was to make sure that anyone who needed them to believe something had the platform to offer the tutelage.

It has been revealed that that’s the place where I think we are failing. We don’t do the tutelage. We say, “There has been a conversation, this is now our truth. And if you don’t adopt that truth, you are somehow opposed to it,” as opposed to, “You haven’t adopted the truth because you don’t know what it means and you don’t understand it and you haven’t experienced it. Let me give you time and space to come in,” or, “You have legitimate disagreement, and maybe on this, we will not be in alignment, but your disagreement should not lead to hostility against my community.”.

The Democratic Socialists of America have attracted a lot of attention recently, but one thing they seem to do is this “belonging” piece. I can’t say I understood this before, but I was talking to someone for a story, and then mentioned the social environment. So here in New York, when people go out to canvas, afterwards, they all go out for beers. The beers are not really the point, but making people feel like they belong to something is.

Yeah. I mean, what they are doing is what works in most effective social movements. During the Vietnam War, one of the most effective protest waves happened at coffee shops. You brought people together around the table, they got to vent about what they were upset about, they went out and protested and then they came back together. People like being liked.

According to recent reports, in terms of belief, how does one do that and not make those who are in that coalition who are particularly vulnerable feel abandoned? Obviously, I mean, this is not the only case, but I’m thinking about the tremendous amount of negative attention brought on the trans community. What do you do when the “belonging” comes in conflict with actually protecting the members of your coalition?

My first position is, if you have a faith that tells you it is okay to cause harm because you feel uncomfortable, I need to understand where your faith lies. Our first responsibility is the protection of difference. And it is to say you don’t have to embrace, but you cannot lift up pitchforks. You cannot demonize, you cannot revile, you cannot scapegoat because all of those are hostile actions of cruelty that not only cause harm to the victim, they diminish your ability to learn. So the worry I have is that too often we sacrifice that education piece because it’s uncomfortable and because it requires defending those you may not be in complete alignment with, and it’s an easier thing to just jump on the bandwagon.

In my caucus, when I was a minority leader, another glitch I had was abortion, and I had two members who were pastors. I was not going to be able to change their ideological position and I wasn’t going to try. But I had these members walk off the floor, instead of voting, on abortion bills. And there were some who got mad and they’re like, “Oh, we should know their position.” I stated, “A yes vote on this bill causes harm, and no vote is a help. Not voting is the same as a no vote. So why do you need them to make a declaration when their declaration of refusing to do harm is progress?” So there’s a complexity that we often elide because we failed to measure what harm looks like, and the path from good to harm is a lot shorter than we want to believe.

Did you work with Angie Nixon during her race?

I feel like she excited a certain element of the base in a way that we haven’t really seen before.

Industry observers note that I contributed and then I went down to Florida, actually did an event at Florida A&M University and did one at Cafe Resistance. I got to know her mama. I knew of her as a state representative. And when I decided to support her campaign, it was because she has always put the work of serving people first. She has built networks, but more importantly, she solves problems.

It has been revealed that when Florida started banning books, she started a bookstore for banned books. That kind of tactical response with strategic intention is often lacking and it has been part of how I try to operate. We’ve got people who are good at being diagnosticians and we’ve got folks who can offer prescriptions and we’ve got people who can actually administer the medicine. And we need more people who are willing to do all three. You need people who are specialists; I’m not saying you don’t, but what she has demonstrated is the capacity to do the three.

In a recent development, have you heard some of the negative commentary after the election about her campaign? I’m thinking about James Carville, for instance—this notion that somehow she was a poor fit for Florida or was a bad candidate. It’s not great. Have you seen any of this?

I have. I don’t read very much of it.

Well, I have thoughts on the fact that we keep thinking the solution to the problem is the thing that failed before. And I believe in experimentation. If you look at my history, I have never been top of mind as the solution to problems. And some of it is timing, some of it is capacity, and some of it is helping change the public imagination, but we’re never going to get what we need if we only use what we’ve always had.

It has been revealed that I just find it interesting that she is attracting negative commentary, from certain quarters, in a way that David Jolly is not, even though they both lost and the margin wasn’t that much between the two of them. She came very, very close to winning, in a state Democrats really didn’t expect to compete in two years ago. And look, I just have to say, you are somebody who in 2018 came really, really close too. You’re both Black women. I just wonder what you make of the critique.

Sources indicate that the critique is easy because Angie Nixon is different. She’s different than what they are used to, and she is different than 250 years of expectation has led us to presume is right. I am excited about Juliana Stratton and Angela Alsobrooks and Lisa Blunt Rochester being in the US Senate. That is an extraordinary thing. Adding Angie Nixon would’ve been an amazing, amazing addition. But for pundits whose sense of success is grounded in past history, she strains the imagination.

It has been revealed that david Jolly ran a smart race. Angie Nixon ran a smart race, and we know that because they came close to winning, but you are never entitled to victory. You are entitled to effort. And this notion that there is some magical formula for what wins in the South got completely obliterated yesterday when Scott Colom won a seat that we haven’t held since 1874. We know that what can win is a combination of a smart candidate, an invested campaign, and an electorate who sees and hears themselves in the story told.

According to recent reports, angie didn’t get that opportunity because she had a late primary and no resources. And to judge her using a metric that was never designed for her is deeply problematic. And it’s not just about her being a Black woman, it’s about how do we win an evolving electorate if all we know is to do what we’ve always done? And so my argument for the Democratic Party is that our notions of electability have to evolve with the democracy that we deserve and that we design, and it cannot be anchored to these sometimes antiquated notions that the only thing we can do is not lose as opposed to let’s try really hard to win by meeting the moment. And I think Angie Nixon did an incredible job of meeting the moment.

And what about you—do you still have ambitions for public office?

Recent findings suggest that do you worry that some of the work you do as a kind of public political strategist (like in this interview, frankly) will conflict at all? When I think about people seeking office, they often try to say as little as possible.

Politics is a tool. It is not an identity for me. It’s a tool. And that’s different. And there are people for whom this is what they do and we need those people. This is not a disparaging comment about others, but for me, it is a tool. It is one of the ways to do the work I believe needs to be done. I think that poverty is immoral. I think it is solvable. I think it is economically inefficient. And for most of my life, the work for me has been about how do you solve this economic poverty? When I got deep in the work, I realized that we also had a moral poverty that we had to contend with, and we have this poverty of imagination. And the problem is you cannot convince people to believe that their problems can be solved if you won’t talk about them.

Recent findings suggest that and in the South, silence is protective. It has been a way to nibble around the edges, but the only people who could be loud about it were the people who could afford volume. And politicians rarely can afford volume. I want things to be better and I’m not willing to forgo any tool that will make that happen. But I’m also not willing to protect my future opportunities by rejecting my current responsibilities.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new update - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear.".

Industry observers note that "If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong.".

Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

According to recent reports, "She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY.".

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

So far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr mentioned it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020.".

I Didn’t Expect Jennifer Love Hewitt’s Intense Take On Reuniting With Ryan Phillippe For 9-1-1

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 9-1-1 franchise is heating up amid the 2026 TV schedule.
  • Hewitt and Phillippe starred together in the first IKWYDLS film, which was released back in 1997.
  • Following speculation that Phillippe and Hewitt would be reuniting, Hewitt recently confirmed that he would indeed guest star on 9-1-1, reprising his Nashville role as Detective Rogue Kelly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 9-1-1 franchise is heating up amid the 2026 TV schedule. While the fall finales of both the Mothership and 9-1-1: Nashville air this week, there's going to be a lot more on the way in the new year. This includes a much-anticipated I Know What You Did Last Summer reunion between Jennifer Love Hewitt and Ryan Phillippe. I'm excited, but what I didn’t expect was Hewitt’s intense take on working with her former co-star again.

Hewitt and Phillippe starred together in the first IKWYDLS film, which was released back in 1997. While Phillippe’s Barry Cox is eventually murdered in the movie, Hewitt’s Julie James becomes the focal point of the sequels. So it’s been close to 30 years since the original movie, and it's great that Barry and Julie are finally back together in some sense.

Following speculation that Phillippe and Hewitt would be reuniting, Hewitt recently confirmed that he would indeed guest star on 9-1-1, reprising his Nashville role as Detective Rogue Kelly. Surprisingly, this is actually the first time that they’ve seen each other since filming wrapped on IKWYDLS, and Hewitt recalled to People just what the atmosphere felt like before the crossover came together. And her take even makes me a bit anxious:.

In a recent development, I was so nervous. I had dry mouth and like a full racy heart. Everybody was like, ‘Are you excited?’ I was like, ‘I feel like I’ve forgotten how to act.’ Yeah, it was amazing. We greeted each other with just a major hug and he was like, ‘This is going to be really fun.’ I mentioned, ‘I think it is.’ And it was just, it was a dream.

I love that even though they’ve worked together before, Hewitt can still have those nerves, and I can’t say I blame her. Reuniting with someone you haven’t seen in years -- even if it's on your own turf -- can be intimidating. It sounds like the mood instantly shifted when Phillippe came to set, in a good way, and it makes me even more excited to see how it all turns out.

Phillippe only joined 9-1-1: Nashville for Season 2, so the fact that the two highlights are already jumping at the chance to do a crossover featuring him and Hewitt is pretty great. Plus, seeing Phillippe and Hewitt together again is like a '90s-infused dream, and it sounds like they had the time of their lives. Hewitt admitted just how much fun they’ve had from seeing the Internet reacting to the news. She also shared how great it’s been to welcome Phillippe to the 9-1-1 Universe, especially after she reunited with Freddie Prinze Jr. for 2025’s I Know What You Did Last Summer:.

In a recent development, he and I have had the best time with people’s reaction. We’ve been DMing going, ‘Did you see it?’ I think we broke the internet. We’ve been having the best time. It was so great because I got to go back and do the movie with Freddie [Prinze Jr.] and sort of have that, and do [our characters] Julie James and Ray again. But this was very different because it was like, [Ryan’s] newly introduced in that universe. I’ve been in this universe for a while. It’s such a safe, lovely place to be with the best people. And he and I have not seen each other since I was 18 years old.

Industry observers note that as for right now, details surrounding the next 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville crossover have not been revealed, and I'm eager to see what brings Rogue to Los Angeles. After trying to track down a serial killer in Nashville who is using biblical plagues, hopefully this trip out West will be a bit lighter for him. Of course, if anyone can help him, it’s Hewitt’s Maddie Buckley-Han, who is arguably the best 9-1-1 dispatcher in LA.

Hopefully, crossover information is confirmed soon, but considering the amount of content Jennifer Love Hewitt has been sharing on her Instagram, she is probably going to keep fans fed for the time being.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that for now, viewers can tune in for the fall finales of 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville, which air this Thursday, November 19, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day with a Hulu subscription. Both demonstrates will then return from their midseason breaks on Thursday, January 7.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the entire Hisense U8 lineup is presently discounted ahead of Black Friday, with prices starting at $797.96 for the 55-inch model (down from $1,424.99) and going up to $2,798.99 for the massive 100-inch version (originally $3,999.99). The discounts also extend to the 65-, 75-, and 85-inch models, with savings of up to $1,200 across the lineup. Regardless of which size you choose, Amazon throws in free delivery to the room of your choice, a service that normally costs $19.99.

Sources indicate that brightness is the U8QG’s main advantage, with the manufacturer estimating up to 5,000 nits of peak brightness, while PCMag measured around 3,200 nits when reviewing the 65-inch model. Actual performance will vary with the picture mode and content, but either figure points to strong highlights in Dolby Vision and HDR10 video. Its Mini-LED local dimming also produces deep blacks, although some light bloom can appear around bright objects on dark backgrounds. Audio-wise, its built-in 4.1.2-channel system, which includes surround channels, a subwoofer, and upward-firing speakers, gives movies more scale than typical TV speakers, though a separate sound system can still offer clearer separation and a broader soundstage.

The U8QG also has plenty to offer gamers using a current-generation console or a capable gaming PC. It supports refresh rates up to 165Hz, variable refresh rate, and AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, with a measured 4.3 milliseconds of input lag at 1080p and 120Hz and 10.1 milliseconds at 4K and 60Hz. Those results should make controls feel responsive, even during fast-paced games. There’s also a side-mounted USB-C port that accepts DisplayPort video, while Google TV handles streaming alongside Apple AirPlay and Google Cast. The biggest inconvenience is the limited selection of three HDMI ports, since a console, soundbar, and streaming device would occupy all of them.

Industry observers note that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

In a recent development, black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry News: You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them.
  • It has been revealed that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress.
  • Industry observers note that it seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

It has been revealed that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a fresh manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a big heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

Industry observers note that it seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," says David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style.".

According to recent reports, that means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," says Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

Sources indicate that in the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to New Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Having to refuel cars in GTA 6 was weirdly one of the most talked about features before launch—I guess people didn't like the idea of having to pull over for gas while being chased by half the Vice City's police department. But the reality is that refuelling cars is something you'll barely find yourself doing.

When your ride does run low on fuel, you can find a gas station on the map via the gas pump symbols:.

Easy, right? And you'll barely have to do it since, just like real life, cars can go quite a long time without refuelling if they have a full tank, even if you're going over 60mph, which I assume you are. Note that if you steal a stranger's car, their tank may nearly be empty already.

According to recent reports, if you're driving an electric car, check the map for recharging stations. Pull up close to one, select "Charge Vehicle," and it'll display the cost. You'll see a quick scene of the readout on the charging station filling the battery to 100%, and when it's done, you can drive away.

Now, the better reason to visit Vice City's fuel stations is that they can repair your vehicle, and if you drive like I do, you'll need this a lot. This is a separate interaction at the same gas pump: on the"Services" menu, just select "Repair" instead. The camera will whoosh into the sky for a moment, and when it returns to ground level your ride will be fixed.

The cost depends on how much damage you've done to your vehicle, but it's well worth it if you want to retain your ride, considering the usual vehicular wear-and-tear that comes with being a professional criminal.

Since you can customise your beloved vehicles at the Mod Shop, or even claim fancier cars by removing their trackers at the Pay 'n' Spray, once you unlock this in the story, keeping your car in good condition is a worthwhile investment.

Taylor Swift’s return to the 2026 CMA Awards was all the talk in Music City — but in a surprising twist, she didn’t take home any trophies.

Ella Langley beat out Swift, 36, on Wednesday, November 18, for Single of the Year, the first award handed out during the celebratory evening.

Swift was nominated for “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy Story 5, while Langley, 27, won for “Choosin’ Texas,” produced by the singer herself, as well as Miranda Lambert and Ben West.

Langley, who was nominated in the same category for her song, “Be Her,” also bested powerhouse singers Lainey Wilson, who hosted the awards show, and Cody Johnson.

Sources indicate that “I love this song,” Langley remarked during her acceptance speech. “We just sat in a room and did our best one afternoon and it is the gift that just keeps on giving.” (Langley walked the red carpet solo after Us previously confirmed that she is dating country singer Tucker Wetmore.).

Recent findings suggest that she gushed, “I’m just grateful to be a part of it. I truly am. I can’t believe this is my life and what’s going on is absolutely insane. I just can’t believe it’s me this is happening to.”.

Swift, for her part, has never won a CMA in the category but she was previously nominated in the award in 2013 for “Highway Don’t Care,” recorded with Tim McGraw and Keith Urban.

It has been revealed that earlier this month, producers revealed that Swift would be taking to the stage for her first performance at the ceremony in 13 years. (The 14-time Grammy winner first attended the CMAs in 2006.).

The special night came after Swift recently traveled to Tennessee and celebrated making music history with her induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

The “Patient Zero” singer officially became the youngest inductee in the prestigious music organization during its annual ceremony on October 26.

Recent findings suggest that “There is no music community like this music community. I know. I checked all the communities. There’s no one doing it,” she said in her speech via Rolling Stone. “Nashville is the place that honed and polished the thing about myself and the thing about my life that I am the most proud of and the most passionate about.”.

Swift continued, “To be here with you and to be getting to have this moment, I am truly grateful, and it just feels like one of those amazing Nashville moments I’m going to revisit on a rainy day.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
